Domestic Politics

Former President Jokowi's son Kaesang Pangarep will contest the 2029 legislative elections in Central Java's Dapil V (Solo area), with the move described as a strategy to build a "kandang gajah" (elephant pen) political base. Analysts identified two main considerations behind Kaesang's decision to run in this constituency, while PAN and Golkar officials said they are ready to compete in what remains a tight electoral battleground. Meanwhile, Jokowi will continue his political tour to East Nusa Tenggara on 31 July.

  • President Prabowo received directives from President Prabowo following Perry Warjiyo's resignation as Bank Indonesia governor, while Commission XI of the DPR is waiting for the president to submit the name of a replacement candidate.
  • PKS's Majelis Syura issued decisions including full support for Prabowo and calls to champion the Palestinian cause.
  • PDIP figures commented on the detention of former Jampidsus Febrie Adriansyah, with the party criticizing special privileges he allegedly received, while Formappi urged the DPR to form a special inquiry committee into the case.
  • PDIP secretary Hasto Kristiyanto responded to polling showing a 30 percent drop in public satisfaction with Prabowo's performance, according to SMRC survey data.
  • PDIP chairwoman Megawati Soekarnoputri said the Kudatuli monument was the result of her contemplation of Soekarno's ideals, and has never forgotten the 27 July 1996 tragedy.
  • Perindo called on its cadres to emulate the spirit of Norway at the World Cup ahead of the 2029 elections, while also urging legislators to be more sensitive to community issues following the Bali mob beating case.
  • PDIP announced it will provide legal assistance to victims of the mob beating incident in Bali.

Foreign Policy & Defence

Indonesia and Papua New Guinea plan to hold ministerial-level talks aimed at deepening bilateral ties between the two neighbouring countries. The meetings are expected to advance cooperation across multiple sectors and strengthen diplomatic relations in the region.

  • The Indonesian embassy in Bogotá promoted Indonesian culture at a Colombian beauty pageant.
  • The Migrant Worker Protection Ministry invited young people to seize global employment opportunities at the Pasim IJF 2026 event.

Other

Bank Indonesia's acting governor pledged policy continuity following the surprise resignation of Governor Perry Warjiyo, with the central bank assuring markets there is no cause for panic. The government has yet to name Warjiyo's successor, while the state holding company Danantara will for the first time participate in the Financial System Stability Committee.

  • Indonesia is lobbying the United States to secure a tariff exemption for palm oil exports amid ongoing trade negotiations.
  • The government announced new electric vehicle incentives explicitly linked to the national car project to boost domestic EV production.
  • The head of the National Food Agency (BGN) announced that 833 MBG kitchens have been permanently closed due to violations, with officials confirming no payments will be made to the suspended facilities and banning the use of subsidized products including Minyakita and 3kg LPG cylinders.
  • The government announced that 35,000 Red and White Cooperatives will begin operations in September as part of economic empowerment efforts.
  • A Bali waste-to-energy plant will reduce emissions and create jobs according to government officials.
